sourceReview.finding: Video/Content is an activated business module; authorized relationships and declared membership eligibility remain authoritative; media delivery is a bounded commodity rail.

dragons.name: Publish → Discover → Watch
dragons.outcome: An authorized staff member publishes one approved on-demand video; an eligible linked member discovers its details and watches it; staff can withdraw it.
dragons.whyFirst: Turns the existing empty library into one complete customer journey and proves content ownership, viewing access and basic staff management before expanding the catalog.

dragons.name: Organized Practice Library
dragons.outcome: Staff organizes videos into simple categories or collections; members find relevant practice by topic, instructor or level with clear details and empty states.
dragons.boundary: No recommendation engine, social features or advanced creator tools.

dragons.name: Media Access Through Existing Memberships
dragons.outcome: Business-approved media eligibility uses existing membership/pass capabilities; members see clear access states and authorized next steps as eligibility changes.
dragons.boundary: No parallel entitlement engine, new payments or invented entitlement promises; reuse an existing purchase path only where supported.

firstBuild.journey: Staff prepares approved video → publishes → linked eligible member browses → opens details → plays → staff unpublishes and future access is denied
include: One on-demand video type in the existing signed-in library
Business-owned title, description, instructor where available, duration and one simple category
Draft and unpublished content unavailable to members
One explicitly approved simple viewing policy using existing account/business linkage
Server-enforced viewing access, not merely hidden buttons; no private source credentials in the browser
Clear loading, unavailable, no-content and access-denied states
Vega proving content and a second-business fixture proving isolated reuse
firstBuild.proposedAccessPolicy: Published V1 videos available to authenticated linked members of that business; proposal for Joe + Chett review, not an approved entitlement policy.
